key_insight: Pauli propagation enables classical pre-training of large, shallow parametrized quantum circuits while leaving target quantum states or samples classically intractable.
engineering_relevance: Moving loss optimization to classical hardware reduces reliance on costly quantum gradient estimation before deploying trained circuits on quantum processors.
method: Propagate observables backward through the circuit to derive an explicit parameter-dependent loss.
Use weight- and degree-based truncation plus pruning heuristics to control propagation cost.
Optimize parameters classically, then deploy the trained circuits on quantum hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two 64-qubit benchmarks—VQE for a two-dimensional Ising model and binary-image generative learning—with trained parameters deployed on IBM's ibm_berlin processor.
watch_item: Truncation and pruning make propagation tractable but can introduce approximation error that requires validation for each circuit and task.
paper_title: Classical Pre-Training of Large Shallow Parametrized Quantum Circuits through Pauli Propagation and deployment on Quantum Hardware
